title: Frostbite
summary: Get them out of the cold and treat any hypothermia first. Only rewarm frostbitten skin if it will not refreeze – then use warm (not hot) water.

callEmergency.headline: Get medical help for frostbite
when: Skin that is white, grey, waxy, hard or blistered
Frostbite on the face, or large areas

steps.title: Treat hypothermia first
steps.text: Move to shelter, remove wet clothing, insulate and warm the whole person.

steps.title: Protect the area
steps.text: Remove rings and tight items. Handle gently and do not let them walk on frostbitten feet if avoidable.

steps.title: Rewarm only if it will not refreeze
steps.text: If there is no risk of refreezing and medical care is delayed, rewarm the area in warm water (about 37–40 °C / 99–104 °F) for 20–30 minutes.
steps.caution: Refreezing after thawing causes much worse damage – if it may refreeze, keep it protected and do not rewarm.

steps.title: Afterwards
steps.text: Cover loosely with dry, clean dressings, separating fingers and toes. Expect pain as it thaws.

doNot: Do not rub or massage the area
Do not use direct dry heat (fires, heaters, hot water bottles)
Do not thaw if there is a risk of refreezing

sources.body: American Heart Association and American Red Cross
sources.title: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid
